body.x: INTERPOL is the world’s largest international police organization, with 196 Member Countries. Created in 1923, it facilitates cross-border police co-operation, and supports and assists all organizations, authorities, and services whose mission is to prevent or combat international crime.

INTERPOL actively encourages applications from women and nationals of member countries that are currently unrepresented among our staff (please click on this link to access the list of countries). Candidates from these countries are particularly encouraged to apply.
INTERPOL’s recruitment process is merit-based hence all hiring decisions are made considering the applicant’s qualifications and the needs of the Organization.
Reporting To: Director of Cabinet and Deputy Director of Cabinet

Only professional experience for which candidates can provide official proof of employment will be considered. Candidates could be requested to provide copies of such official documents prior to interviews/test.
* Subsequent extension to this post will be subject to the terms of the Organization’s Staff Manual, to satisfactory performance and to availability of funds.

Tests/interviews in connection to this selection procedure will take place approximately 1/2 weeks after the deadline for applications. Applicants are kindly requested to plan their availability during this period accordingly, in case they are short-listed.
Selected candidates will be expected to report for duty approximately two to three months after receiving an offer of employment at the latest.
This selection exercise may be used to generate a reserve list of suitable candidates that may be used to address Organization's similar staffing needs in the future.
SUMMARY OF THE ASSIGNED DUTIES, INCLUDING GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF THE POST

Under the guidance of the Head and Deputy Head of Cabinet, the incumbent provides a full range of high-level administrative assistance and analytical support to the Secretary General, the Director and Deputy Director of Cabinet.

Provide administrative assistance to the Secretary General under the guidance of the Director of Cabinet and the Deputy Director of Cabinet and deal with day-to-day matters concerning the Cabinet in close cooperation with his/her peers. This includes, inter alia:
• Ensure drafting, handling, logging and tracking of all in and outgoing correspondence, including follow-up with the relevant Directorates.
• Draft official and social correspondence either form templates, brief oral instruction or own research or knowledge of the organization’s operation.
• Update contact records following correspondence received and sent by the Secretary General.
• Review letters prepared by Directorates for the signature of the Secretary General.
• Ensure the transmission (both electronic mailing and paper where applicable) of letters, messages, etc., signed by the Secretary General.
• Draft other documents of the Secretary General, including messages to staff, memoranda and coordinate their translation.

• Prepare all necessary documentation concerning engagement of the Secretary General’s agenda under the guidance of the Director of Cabinet and the Deputy Director of Cabinet: appointments, internal meetings, visitors, interviews, missions etc.;
• Deal with external telephone calls and internal requests from staff and take appropriate action as necessary;

• Ensure that documentation is traced and available upon request through an efficient filing system, enabling the easy retrieval of documents to assist the Secretary General, the Director of Cabinet, the Deputy Director of Cabinet and other officials from the Organization who may request a document linked with the Cabinet’s activities;
• Check deadlines of pending issues, follow-up on commitments and actions resulting from missions and visits of the Secretary General.
Provide administrative assistance to the Director of Cabinet and the Deputy Director of Cabinet.

• Perform secretarial duties and administrative assistance for the Director of Cabinet and the Deputy Director of Cabinet by ensuring the efficient preparation and administration of the correspondence and documentation needed for the daily work of the Secretary General;
• Support and troubleshoot immediate issues that arise;

• Prepare all necessary documentation concerning engagement of the Secretary General’s agenda and the agenda of the Director of Cabinet and the Deputy Director of Cabinet: appointments, internal meetings, visitors, interviews, missions etc.;
• Ensure confidential and official note taking at meetings and the drafting of Minutes.
• Perform all other duties as assigned by the hierarchy;

• Stand in for secretariat duties performed by the Executive Office of the Secretary General when needed to ensure the smooth running of the Office, particularly during absences of other members of the Executive Office.
• Three to four years’ education at a University or equivalent higher education diploma in Public Administration, secretariat or other related discipline.
• At least 10 years’ experience in the area is required if the post holder does not have the required level of education.
• Proficiency in English and fluency in French is essential.
• Knowledge of other official INTERPOL language (Arabic or Spanish) would be an additional asset.
• At least three years of professional experience in providing executive level support at leadership level (ex: Head of international organization, CEO of private company, Minister Cabinet).
• Experience in an international environment will be considered an asset.
• Proficient writing skills and excellent proofreading skills are essential;
• High level of autonomy and capacity to solve problems that arise under short time constraints;
• Ability to cope with sudden increases in workload, and high degree of availability;
• Ability to work in a team and to maintain good relations with members of the General Secretariat;
• Attention to detail and organization skills;
As part of our commitment to transparency throughout our recruitment process, INTERPOL's Staff Manual Regulation 11.4: Age-limit, which states that:

'Officials of the Organization shall not normally be retained in service beyond the age of 65 years. The Secretary General may, in exceptional cases and in the interests of the Organization, extend this age limit, in which case he shall inform the official concerned sufficiently in advance.'

Given this Regulation and in case candidates reach the age of 65 during the potential duration of the appointment, should they be selected for the position and the process proceed to appointment, the employment period may be affected by this regulatory limit and may therefore not extend for the full standard contract duration as published in the vacancy notice.
We are sharing this information to ensure transparency at this stage of the process.
This position is no longer open.
